steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Dactylic hexameter is the metre of epic poetry: six feet per line, each foot being a dactyl (- uu) or spondee (--). The final foot is always a spondee or trochee. | Key Fact: A dactyl is one long syllable followed by two short syllables (dum-di-di). A spondee is two long syllables (dum-dum). | Key Fact: The caesura is a natural pause within a hexameter line, usually in the third foot, creating rhythm and structure. | Key Fact: Elision occurs when a word ending in a vowel runs into a word beginning with a vowel or h-: the final vowel is not pronounced separately.
